repairs.after: {"q": "v4 drops support for one legacy protocol on upstreams. Which protocol is it, and how many upstreams are known to still use it?", "answer": "HTTP/1.0; 17 upstreams are known to still speak it", "accept": ["17 upstreams known to be on HTTP/1.0, which v4 no longer supports", "seventeen upstreams on old HTTP", "HTTP/1.0 support dropped, 17 known upstreams affected"]}
repairs.rationale: The first pass retargeted q5 from breaking_changes (HTTP/1.0 upstream support, 17 upstreams) to exemptions (30 days at a time, 22 granted, 9 to three teams). The cold pass it was fixing is real, but the retarget left breaking_changes graded by no question in status_update-04: q1 grades migration_progress, q2 security_driver, q3 codemod_coverage, q4 build_enforcement plus eol_date, and q5 then grades exemptions. Every brief carries exactly five questions (FROZEN.json: 40 briefs, 200 questions), so this was a swap, and it swapped out the fact the audience of this document - the engineering leads of every consuming team - most needs to act on. The cold pass was a key defect, not a property of the question. I reproduced it: the old accept[1] 'HTTP/1.0, 17 upstreams' reduces to the two-token lexical key ['http/1.0','upstreams'], and the cold reply 'v4 drops HTTP/1.0 support for upstreams.' supplies both - the protocol from world knowledge, 'upstreams' from the stem - so it scored 2/2 without ever producing 17. So the original target is restored and the keys are rebuilt around the one part of the answer world knowledge cannot supply: the count. Three properties hold now. Every digit-bearing key requires {1.0, 17} or more, so the protocol alone never scores. No key has a short lexical list: the canonical is five words needing four, and the two digit-bearing accepts are six words needing five, which the cold reply cannot reach. The spelled-out rendering gets its own key, 'seventeen upstreams on old HTTP', deliberately digit-free - a spelled key that still wrote 'HTTP/1.0' would carry the number set {1.0}, which is a subset of the cold reply's numbers and would reopen the hole through the numeric branch. With no digits the numeric branch is skipped and the key is three tokens, all required (0.8*3 = 2.4), one of them 'seventeen' - unobtainable without the document. Verified against a replica of tools/comprehension.py. Pass: HTTP/1.0, HTTP 1.0 and HTTP1.0 spellings with 17, a terse 'HTTP/1.0 - 17 upstreams', a colon-list rendering, and two spelled-out 'seventeen' renderings - eight in total. Fail: the cold reply the verify pass used, two other cold variants, the stem echo, a confident guess with the wrong count, a count-without-protocol reply, two protocol-without-count replies, and NOT STATED. Cost of this choice, stated plainly: exemptions goes back to being ungraded, which is where the frozen eval had it. Between the two, breaking_changes is the fact whose loss a reader of the document would feel, and it is now gradeable without the cold pass that motivated the swap.

repairs.after: {"q": "How many of the consuming multiproducts have moved to v4, out of how many total, and how many remain on v3?", "answer": "388 of 1,000 are on v4 (38.8%); 612 remain on v3", "accept": ["388/1,000 on v4, 612 on v3", "38.8% migrated — 388 of 1,000; 612 left", "388 on v4, 39%, 612 on v3", "388/1000 on v4, 612 on v3"]}
repairs.rationale: Found by running the task's own check - write a lazy wrong reply and confirm it fails - across the rest of this brief. Pre-existing rather than repair-induced, but it is the archetype the verify pass named, and it sits two items away from the q5 repair. accept[2] '388 on v4 (about 39%), 612 still on v3' reduces to the lexical key ['about','still'] and accept[3] '612 remaining of 1,000, 388 done' reduces to ['remaining','done']. Both are two generic words, both are matched by substring, and I measured three number-free replies scoring CORRECT on a question that asks for three counts: 'The migration is still about halfway.', 'The remaining work is mostly done.', and 'About a third of teams are still on the old version.' Only those two accepts change; the canonical and the first two accepts are untouched. accept[2] becomes '388 on v4, 39%, 612 on v3' - every token is three characters or shorter, so its lexical word list is empty and the lexical branch is disabled outright, while the number set {388, 39, 4, 612, 3} that made the key worth having (the rounded 39% rendering) is preserved exactly. accept[3] becomes '388/1000 on v4, 612 on v3', whose only lexical token is the eight-character '388/1000' - specific enough that the only reply containing it is a correct one - and whose number set {388, 1000, 4, 612, 3} restores the no-comma rendering, which previously reached CORRECT only through the ['remaining','done'] sieve and would otherwise have been lost: normalise turns '1,000' into '1 000', so the comma and no-comma conventions are different number sets and each needs a key. Verified: nine lazy replies fail (the three above, the stem echo, the topic sentence, numerator-only, remainder-only, a wrong-numbers reply, and NOT STATED) and seven correct renderings pass (comma, no-comma, rounded 39% in both comma conventions, slash, reordered, and full prose).
